narrative.northStar: The Language Set Out as a Book and a Chart
narrative.overview:
The site is a language's home page done properly and a tour that teaches the whole language, and it is set the way a good technical book is set: a cool white paper, one ink, a book serif for everything that is read and its sibling monospace for everything that is run. Two devices belong to teaching a language and nothing else, and they are the system's signature: the grammar drawn as railroad diagrams (in the tour only), and the whole language laid out as one periodic-table chart of 74 tiles in nine chapter colours. Every slide carries its own tile beside its title, so a chapter has a colour and 74 slides stop looking like one.

Density is a book's: an 18px body at a 66ch measure, generous paper between sections (128px on the front page), two columns where the explanation sits beside the programs it explains. Colour is rationed hard. Chapter colours only ever fill a tile; amber is the way on and where the reader is, and nothing else. Nothing moves: no entrance animation, no positional motion, only a 160ms colour change on the button, pills and tiles. The site ships no JavaScript beyond the playground's one script, so every state the design has (the reader's scheme, read slides, the current station) is drawn by CSS from what HTML and the server already know; only running an example needs the script.

Confirmed rejections: the SaaS landing page (gradient hero, feature-card rows, glow), a literal bee-and-honey theme, cream paper, and railroad drawing outside the tour.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper (never cream), one ink, flat surfaces separated by paper rather than lines.
Source Serif 4 for headings and prose, Source Code Pro for programs, tiles and tokens; both embedded, nothing fetched.
Nine muted chapter colours, each with a deeper read shade, filling tiles only.
Amber on exactly two things: the one primary button and the reader's current station.
Square tiles and panels; pills only for links that act as buttons; circles only for stations and drawn markers.
Light and dark follow the system, with a no-JS cookie switch in the running head.

rules.name: The Tile-Only Rule
rules.body: Chapter colours fill tiles and nothing else: never text, borders, backgrounds of sections, or underlines. If it is not a tile (or a key swatch naming a tile's colour), it is paper or ink.

rules.name: The Two Ambers Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the way on (the single primary button) and where the reader is (the current station). A third amber element dilutes both. Hover underlines in amber are the only permitted trace beyond these.

rules.name: The Read Shade Rule
rules.body: Read state is `:visited` turning a tile to its chapter's deeper shade. It changes colour only, needs no script, and is the whole progress system on the chart.

rules.name: The Serif-Reads, Mono-Runs Rule
rules.body: Anything a reader could type into a `.hive` file (programs, tokens, commands, tile symbols, terminals in diagrams) is set in the monospace; everything else is the serif. Rule names in diagrams are serif italic, because they are names, not text to type.

rules.name: The Bold Keyword Rule
rules.body: Syntax highlighting is typographic first: keywords and builtins in bold, comments in the serif italic, colour only for strings and literals. Names, types and calls stay in ink.

rules.name: The Inline-Direction Rule
rules.body: `hive.ui` writes a row's direction as an inline `style`, so responsive overrides of flex direction, alignment and gap use `!important`, inside the responsive block only and for that purpose only. Nowhere else does the stylesheet use `!important` (besides the reduced-motion reset).

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. A surface is paper, a shade off paper, or a chapter fill; edges are ink strokes or nothing.

dos: **Do** keep amber to the one primary pill and the current station; everything else that needs emphasis uses ink, weight or an underline.
**Do** fill tiles (chart, slide tile, reads tiles, key swatches) with chapter colours and let `:visited` turn them to the read shade.
**Do** set every program, token, command and tile symbol in Source Code Pro with ligatures off, and everything read in Source Serif 4.
**Do** use the ink focus ring (2px solid ink, 3px offset), or the inset 2px ink ring on filled tiles.
**Do** keep every interactive state in HTML and CSS: `:visited`, `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, server round-trips and the theme cookie.
**Do** draw marks (chevrons, stations, the theme circle, list dots) with CSS or the canvas at the 2px stroke weight.
**Do** let code panels and diagrams scroll sideways with scroll shades instead of shrinking or widening the column.
**Do** keep a slide's railroad figures inside its grammar fold, closed by default, so the slide opens on prose and programs.
**Do** hold all text, and ink on every chapter fill and read shade, at 4.5:1 or better in both schemes.
donts: **Don't** use chapter colours for text, borders, section backgrounds or decoration.
**Don't** add a second amber element, an amber focus ring or amber text on paper.
**Don't** add drop shadows, gradients as decoration, glow, or feature-card rows.
**Don't** use cream or warm paper; the paper is cool.
**Don't** draw railroad diagrams outside the tour.
**Don't** use arrow characters or icon glyphs for direction or status; draw them.
**Don't** add hairlines between sections; only table rows get rules.
**Don't** animate position or add entrance motion; colour changes at 160ms are the only motion.
**Don't** use `!important` except to take back `hive.ui`'s inline row direction, alignment and gap at a breakpoint.
**Don't** ship JavaScript beyond the playground's one script, external fonts, or any asset not embedded in the binary (the playground's compiled programs and Go's `wasm_exec.js` excepted).
